t: You're on Spring Gardens, a short dead-end street at the south-east edge of St. James's. It crosses the east end of The Mall, between Admiralty Arch and Trafalgar Square, and backs onto Whitehall, Horse Guards Parade and Green Park. The name comes from Sir William Spring, a Whig Member of Parliament for Suffolk. Over the years several people have lived here, including Henry William Stanhope. Admiral Sir Charles Eden, who became Second Naval Lord, and Hugh Hamersley both died on this street.
